audit_letter: "M. Silvestri — The manifests for the Sfax sailings do not match my ledger, and the shortfall walks on your legs. Come to my office at midnight with your books, or I bring both to the harbor board. — H.A." (Found under Aubert's blotter, annotated in his hand: 'midnight.')
briefing: Harbor police memorandum, 8:15 AM. The Hôtel Majestic holds its dead man the way a fist holds water, and the shipping line wants this buried before Friday's sailing. Henri Aubert, owner of the hotel, was found at his office desk at 7:40 AM by the maid, with the house doctor already writing 'heart' on the slip. The harbor ledger lies open with a page razored out, and the office safe is forty thousand francs light, so you will forgive me for doubting the doctor. Three people crossed that office's shadow last night: Silvestri, his clerk; Yasmine, his singer; and Bilal, his watchman. Work the hotel and the quay. Speak to everyone twice. Do not let the line sail without your permission. — K.

evidence.description: A squat anisette glass on Aubert's blotter, a finger of cloudy liquor left. Under the anise there is a second taste the doctor will not name — the dispensary man will: sleeping drops, enough to fold a sixty-year-old man over his own desk.
evidence.name: Dosed anisette glass
evidence.proves: Aubert was drugged before death. This was not his heart giving out at the desk.

evidence.description: The house doctor's slip, amended and re-amended: 'pupils constricted' written, then crossed out, then 'heart' written over it in a steadier hand. A man does not cross out his own observation unless someone asked him to.
evidence.name: Doctor's slip
evidence.proves: The doctor saw drugging signs and buried them. The 'heart failure' is bought.

evidence.description: The harbor ledger, open on the desk, one page razored out so cleanly the binding barely shows it. The surviving page ends mid-sentence: '…the Sfax cargo, per M.S., condemned and—'. Whoever cut it came for a name, not for money.
evidence.name: Razored ledger
evidence.proves: Proof was stolen, not merely money. Someone's name was on that page.

evidence.description: Two bills of lading from the harbormaster's hut, both in the same clerk's careful hand — and both misspelling 'quarantine' as 'quarentine'. The hand matches Silvestri's sailing papers. Condemned cargo walked through the quay on these two sheets.
evidence.name: Forged manifests
evidence.proves: Silvestri forged cargo papers. Aubert's audit would have hanged him — motive in ink.

evidence.description: The hotel dispensary book, kept in the bar drawer. Last line, 9:00 PM: 'Sleeping drops, 1 phial — M. Silvestri, for the crossing.' The phial has not come back. The drug in Aubert's glass had to come from somewhere, and the book says where.
evidence.name: Dispensary book
evidence.proves: Silvestri held the exact drops found in Aubert's glass, signed out hours before midnight.

evidence.description: A torn Cinéma L'Étoile stub for the late show, seat row C — and across it the crescent of Yasmine's lipstick, Corail Brûlé, which she will name herself as if it were evidence against her. The singer was in the dark with two hundred strangers, whatever she says about her pillow.
evidence.name: Cinema ticket stub
evidence.proves: Yasmine Ben Ammar was out that night. Her midnight-bed alibi is a lie — and liars near stairs saw things.

evidence.description: A thousand-franc note from the quay café's till, breakfast trade. Its serial belongs to the safe's recorded run — the harbor bank confirms it by wire. Bilal Haddad spent it at dawn, and the café boy remembers the shaking hand.
evidence.name: Café banknote
evidence.proves: The safe was emptied before dawn and Bilal spent from it after. Theft after death — not murder, but a lie that needs breaking.

evidence.description: A lump of sealing wax under the service stair's loose step, holding the clean impression of a service key — and beside it, pressed like a signature, the mark of Silvestri's seal ring. A copied key explains the ajar door better than a ghost does.
evidence.name: Waxed key impression
evidence.proves: Someone copied the service-stair key, and Silvestri's ring signed the wax. Means of quiet entry.

locations.description: Aubert's office above the lobby: blotter, cold anisette, the razored ledger. The doctor wants the sheet pulled up and the matter closed.
locations.name: Hotel office

locations.description: The Majestic bar after closing: stacked glasses, the dispensary drawer, Yasmine's empty stage. The barman polishes one glass and remembers everything.
locations.name: Hotel bar

locations.description: Dawn on the quay: harbormaster's hut, café with the till, gulls over condemned cargo that should never have landed.
locations.name: Marina quay

locations.description: The Cinéma L'Étoile after the late show: torn stubs in the sawdust, row C, and the square beyond where a singer smoked till one.
locations.name: Cinéma L'Étoile

locations.description: The hotel's service stair: a loose step, sealing wax, and a door that was ajar at five in the morning.
locations.name: Service stair

suspects.alibi: In my room above the chandlery from eleven. Seasick in advance — I am a poor sailor for a sailing man.

contradictions.response: For the crossing. Friday's sailing — ask the line. Half of Tunis signs that book before a voyage.
Clerks copy, monsieur. My hand is on a hundred papers. Find me the one that kills, if your eyes are so sharp.
(The courtesy goes out of him like a snuffed lamp.) Seal rings press many things. Wax. Letters. Nothing.

suspects.description: Cargo clerk, Ligne Sfaxienne. Forty-five, jacket buttoned, papers in order, courtesy like a drawn curtain.
suspects.dossier: Marco Silvestri has clerked the Sfax line's Tunis cargo for six years. Two bills of lading in his hand misspell 'quarantine' the same way; condemned cargo walked the quay on them. He sails — he says — on Friday, one-way passage to Palermo already paid. He signed the dispensary book at 9 PM. Aubert's midnight summons was under his blotter.
suspects.name: Marco Silvestri

topics.response: In my room above the chandlery from eleven. Read the regulations, took my drops, slept the sleep of the documented. Next question.
The hotel is my client six years. Monsieur Aubert trusted me with his quay, his manifests, his midnight hours. Whatever the harbor whispers about audits, I was his man.
The Palermo packet, Friday. Personal business, long postponed. My papers are in order — everything about me is in order.

suspects.voice: Elaborate courtesy, long sentences, quotes regulations. Goes flat and short when the manifests come up.

suspects.alibi: In bed by midnight, alone, asleep. Ask my pillow.

contradictions.response: (She looks at the stub a long time, then laughs once, joylessly.) Row C. Corail Brûlé. Very well — I was not abed, monsieur l'inspecteur. I sat in the dark with two hundred strangers because my own room had Aubert's shouting still in it. And since you count my sins: past midnight I smoked in the square, and at half twelve, perhaps, a man came down the service stair with a folio under his arm. Jacket on. It was Silvestri, and I said nothing, because a singer loitering near a dead man's stair loses her contract. There. Are you fed?

suspects.description: Hotel bar singer. Thirty-four, Corail Brûlé lipstick, proverbs when nervous and steel when cornered.
suspects.dossier: Yasmine Ben Ammar has sung the Majestic bar for two seasons. Aubert 'lent' her contract money she cannot repay; they quarreled at 11 PM in front of the barman. Her lipstick is Corail Brûlé. She was seen leaving the Cinéma L'Étoile's late show and bought no ticket — the usher waves singers in.
suspects.name: Yasmine Ben Ammar

topics.response: In bed by midnight, alone, asleep. My pillow will swear it, and my pillow never lies before noon.
About money he lent my contract, yes, at eleven, in front of everyone — I do nothing quietly, monsieur, it is my profession. Hate him a little? Yes. Kill him? With what, high notes?

topics.prompt: Anybody out at the cinema late?
topics.response: The late show lets out near one, they say. I was abed. The square is for smokers and policemen.

suspects.voice: Crisp patter, half French, half courtesy; proverbs when nervous, steel when cornered.

suspects.alibi: Rounds at five, sir. Door locked, sir. Reported at seven-forty.

contradictions.response: (He stands at attention and cries standing at attention, sir.) I never touched him, sir, on my sister's eyes. At five the door stood ajar — ajar, not locked, sir, remember that — and he was cold, and the safe stood empty, and there were banknotes on the floor, and I — I took three, sir. Three. I straightened the desk because my hands needed the work. I spent one at the café because my sister eats, sir. Write that I never touched him.

suspects.description: Night watchman, Hôtel Majestic. Twenty-eight, cap straight, rulebook memorized, hands that will not stop shaking.
suspects.dossier: Bilal Haddad has watched the Majestic's nights for two years and never lost a key. He sends his pay to his sister in Sfax. He found the office at 5 AM and reported it 'locked' at 7:40 with the maid. The café boy remembers his shaking hand and a thousand-franc note.
suspects.name: Bilal Haddad

topics.response: Rounds at two, sir, rounds at five, sir. Doors, stairs, the quay gate. By the book, sir, always by the book.

The maid screamed, sir. The door was locked — locked, sir, remember that — and Monsieur Aubert was cold at his desk, and the safe stood empty, and I stood in the doorway, sir. I never went in. I never touched nothing.

topics.prompt: You sure you never touched anything in there?
topics.response: Never touched nothing, sir. Not a sheet, not a glass, nothing, sir.

suspects.voice: Short formal sentences, 'sir' to everyone. Repeats the rulebook when frightened. Lies once, badly.

testimonies.text: Bilal's account, signed: office door ajar (not locked) at 5 AM, no answer; safe already empty; took three banknotes afterward and straightened the desk. Fixes death before 5 AM and entry by key, not force.
testimonies.title: Bilal's timeline

testimonies.text: Yasmine's account, signed: at about 12:40 AM from the square she saw Marco Silvestri, jacket on with a folio under his arm, come down the service stair toward the quay. Puts Silvestri awake, dressed, and at the scene inside the death window.
testimonies.title: Yasmine's sighting

title: The Tunis Ledger
